annotations.text:
KIONEL — institutional light.

Ground #FBFAF7 · ink #111318 · one accent #1B3A63.
Green #2E7D5B only ever means verified.

No rounded corners anywhere. Depth comes from a hard offset shadow that collapses on press — never from blur or glow.

Type: Source Serif 4 (display) · IBM Plex Sans (body) · IBM Plex Mono (every number).

Motion is a table, not a mood: one easing curve, four durations, 18px travel, 80ms stagger.

Scroll choreography runs in a fixed order — smooth scroll, text reveal, stagger, one pinned section, hover, shallow depth.

Heavy WebGL is deliberately out: a scene that stalls on a factory tablet costs more trust than it buys.

The SAS second factor no longer uses emoji.

Emoji render differently on Apple, Google and Samsung — a comparison factor that looks different on the two devices being compared is a real defect, not a style issue.

Replaced with 32 drawn marks: same 5 bits per symbol, identical on every platform.

Pointer response is limited to two places: the primary action leans toward the cursor, and the hero module field has a two-layer parallax.

No custom cursor, no cursor trail, no tilt on cards. In an institutional context a cursor that behaves unexpectedly reads as a toy.

You cannot sell access to software that runs entirely on the buyer's device — a licence check there is theatre, and gating a security feature would make the free tier dangerous.

So the model sells the three things that cannot be copied: the legal right to embed, the evidence that it works, and someone answering when it does not.

Only the pilot is sellable today. The other two tiers stay marked as not-yet by design.
